universal.label: Police Emergency (110) / Fire & Ambulance (119)
universal.description: Japan uses 110 for Police and 119 for Fire & Ambulance. Both lines provide 24x7 three-way interpretation for foreign visitors.

categories.name: Police & Coast Guard
categories.description: 110 Police emergency, #9110 police consultation, and 118 Japan Coast Guard.

numbers.label: Police Emergency Dispatch (Keisatsu)
numbers.audience: Anyone reporting a crime, traffic accident, theft, or urgent safety threat in Japan.
numbers.whenToUse: Dial 110 immediately for crimes or traffic collisions (even minor accidents require a 110 police report for insurance).

numbers.label: Japan Coast Guard Maritime Emergency
numbers.audience: Anyone witnessing or involved in an accident at sea, coastal drowning, or maritime crime.
numbers.whenToUse: Dial 118 immediately for marine search and rescue around Japanese coastlines.

numbers.label: Police Consultation Hotline (Non-Emergency)
numbers.audience: Residents seeking police advice on stalking, consumer trouble, cyber harassment, or non-urgent concerns.
numbers.whenToUse: Dial #9110 when you need police consultation before an issue becomes a 110 emergency.

categories.name: Medical & Ambulance
categories.description: 119 Emergency Ambulance and #7119 urgent medical triage.

numbers.label: Emergency Ambulance (Kyūkyūsha)
numbers.audience: Anyone experiencing acute illness, severe injury, stroke, cardiac symptoms, or medical trauma.
numbers.whenToUse: Dial 119 and state 'Kyūkyū desu' (It is a medical emergency) followed by your location. Multilingual interpretation is available.

numbers.label: Emergency Medical Consultation Center
numbers.audience: Patients unsure whether to call a 119 ambulance or visit an after-hours clinic.
numbers.whenToUse: Dial #7119 to consult nurses and doctors on symptom urgency and open night/holiday hospitals.
numbers.coverage: Tokyo, Osaka, Sapporo, Yokohama, Fukuoka & major prefectures

numbers.label: Fire & Rescue Dispatch (Kaji)
numbers.audience: Anyone reporting a fire, gas leak, smoke, or trapped person.
numbers.whenToUse: Dial 119 and state 'Kaji desu' (It is a fire) along with the address or nearest landmark.

categories.name: Women & Child Safety
categories.description: 189 Child Guidance Center abuse line and #8008 DV consultation.

numbers.label: Child Guidance Center Abuse Hotline (Ichihayaku)
numbers.audience: Children experiencing abuse, parents struggling, or neighbors suspecting child maltreatment.
numbers.whenToUse: Dial 189 to be routed immediately to the nearest Child Guidance Center for urgent child protection.

numbers.label: DV Consultation Plus (Domestic Violence Hotline)
numbers.audience: Anyone experiencing domestic or partner violence in Japan (multilingual chat/phone support).
numbers.whenToUse: Call 0120-279-889 (24x7) or #8008 for confidential shelter and protection support.

categories.name: Disaster & Highway
categories.description: 171 Earthquake Disaster Message Dial, #9910 Road Emergency, and JNTO Tourist Hotline.

numbers.label: MLIT Road Emergency Dial (Expressways & National Roads)
numbers.audience: Drivers encountering fallen rocks, road cave-ins, debris, or hazards on expressways and national highways.
numbers.whenToUse: Dial #9910 to report road hazards and obstructions directly to highway management centers.

numbers.label: Japan Visitor Hotline (JNTO Multilingual Emergency Support)
numbers.audience: International travellers in Japan needing emergency assistance, earthquake/typhoon info, or medical translation.
numbers.whenToUse: Call anytime in English, Chinese, Korean, or Japanese during disasters, illness, or emergencies.
